title: xAPI Statement Builder
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Experience API
xAPI
Learning Analytics
Student Data Privacy
Intelligent Textbooks
description: Build an Experience API (xAPI) statement from an actor, a verb, and an object. The statement is shown as a sentence and as valid xAPI JSON. A toggle swaps the anonymous session ID for a typed student name to show that the actor field is what turns an anonymous, aggregable statement into per-student data. Nothing is stored or transmitted.

educational.topic: Experience API statements and student data privacy
learningObjectives: Construct a valid actor-verb-object xAPI statement.
Identify which field, if populated with a real name, would cross into regulated per-student data.
prerequisites: Has read the definitions of Experience API and learning record store

controls.label: Actor
controls.description: anonymous-session-4471, anonymous-session-8820, or Type a name...

controls.label: Use real student name instead of session ID
controls.description: Switches the actor between an anonymous session ID and a typed name

controls.label: Student name
controls.description: Enabled when the real-name toggle is on; up to 30 characters

assumptions: The actor is identified by an xAPI account object (homePage plus name)
completed and answered use ADL vocabulary verb IRIs; hovered and clicked use IRIs defined under the example.org placeholder domain
Activity IRIs use the example.org placeholder domain
limitations: No statement is stored or sent to a learning record store
Optional xAPI properties such as result, context, and timestamp are not shown

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: The learner constructs statements and manipulates the one field that changes a statement's privacy status
keyQuestions: Which of the three parts decides whether a statement identifies a person?
What can anonymous statements still tell an author when they are aggregated?
commonMisconceptions: Collecting interaction data always means tracking individual students
The verb or the object is what makes a statement sensitive
assessmentOpportunities: Build statements for three described events and name the field that changes when a real name is used
